goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — Listener is gated on the V1 flag but management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever V2 is on, so with both flags enabled ClientRemovedEvent calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled which throws UnsupportedOperationException and client deletion fails.

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), the ClientRemovedEvent handler calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). In this diff, MgmtPermissionsV2 overrides clients() to return ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) throws UnsupportedOperationException. Therefore, if management(...) can return MgmtPermissionsV2 while this listener is active (e.g., when V2 is enabled alongside the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ gate used here), a client deletion event would trigger an UnsupportedOperationException and break deletion cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — With only V2 enabled, nothing cleans up FGAP v2 per-client resources and permissions when a client is deleted, so stale resources and policies pile up; no test covers client removal with a per-client permission.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:213 — When a per-client resource exists, only that resource is evaluated and all-Clients grants are never consulted, so adding any per-client permission (e.g. view) silently revokes an existing all-clients manage/configure/map-roles grant for that client.

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel,String), the code first looks up a per-client resource by name (client.getId()). If it exists, it evaluates permissions only against that single resource and immediately returns based on that result. The “all-clients” (resource-type) resource is only consulted in the branch where the per-client resource is null (fallback to getResourceTypeResource). Therefore, if an all-clients grant exists (e.g., MANAGE) and later any per-client resource is created (e.g., by adding a VIEW permission), subsequent checks for MANAGE/CONFIGURE/etc. on that client will ignore the all-clients grant and can incorrectly deny access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:219 — getResourceTypeResource returns null when realm admin permissions are disabled or the Clients type resource is missing (e.g. realms initialized before this schema change), so findByResource(server, null) / resource.getScopes() throw NPE on the permission path.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:109 — A "manage all clients" grant also grants canManageClientScopes/canManage(ClientScopeModel), letting a delegated client admin edit realm-wide shared client scopes and protocol mappers that affect every other client (privilege escalation across clients).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in `ClientPermissionsV2`, `canManageClientScopes()` returns `true` when the caller has the global clients permission `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (method at ~109), and `canManage(ClientScopeModel)` simply delegates to `canManageClientScopes()`. This does indeed broaden a “manage all clients” grant into the ability to manage realm-level client scopes. However, from the diff alone it’s not provable this is an unintended security defect (the interface Javadoc added in this PR explicitly documents that V2 treats `MANAGE` as sufficient for managing client scopes). The concern is real and diff-grounded as a permission-model scope/architecture issue, but not verifiably a bug without requirements stating client-scope management must be separately permissioned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:148 — canExchangeTo and the V1 policy/permission accessors throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2, so token-exchange checks and the client management-permissions endpoints return 500 instead of a clean deny, and the schema has no token-exchange scope at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces `ClientPermissionsV2` with multiple overridden methods (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, and many V1-style permission/policy accessors like `managePermission`, `viewPermission`, `resource`, `setPermissionsEnabled`) that unconditionally `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. If any existing admin endpoints or internal flows call these methods under V2 (e.g., token-exchange checks or client permission-management endpoints), that would surface as a server error rather than a controlled denial. Also, the updated `AdminPermissionsSchema` adds the `CLIENTS` resource type with scopes `{CONFIGURE, MANAGE, MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, VIEW}` and does not include any token-exchange scope, so V2 cannot express token-exchange permissions via the schema. However, the specific claim that endpoints "return 500" is not directly verifiable from this diff alone (call sites are not shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:91 — V2 canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles skip the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin-role shortcut that canManage/canView keep, so built-in client admins may lose role mapping under V2.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2`, `canManage(ClientModel)` and `canManageClientScopes()` explicitly preserve the legacy admin-role shortcut (`root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)`), and `canView(ClientScopeModel)` preserves `VIEW_CLIENTS/MANAGE_CLIENTS` shortcuts. However, `canMapRoles(ClientModel)`, `canMapCompositeRoles(ClientModel)`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` only call `hasPermission(client, <scope>)` and do not include any `AdminRoles` shortcut. This inconsistency means callers who rely on built-in admin roles (e.g., `MANAGE_CLIENTS`) could be denied role-mapping operations under V2 unless explicit authz permissions are created.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:83 — getOrCreateResource returns any resource matched by findById before checking resourceType, and Users and Clients share manage/view/map-roles, so a Clients-typed permission given a Users resource id grants user-level scopes (cross-type confusion).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a second resource type (CLIENTS) to AdminPermissionsSchema and extends getOrCreateResource() to resolve client IDs (resolveClient) similarly to users. If getOrCreateResource() (as the finding cites at ~line 83 in the unchanged portion) returns an existing authorization Resource immediately when resourceStore.findById(id, ...) matches, it would do so without validating that the found Resource’s type matches the requested resourceType. With both USERS and CLIENTS now present and sharing overlapping scopes (e.g., manage/view/map-roles), returning a Resource of the wrong type could cause cross-type permission evaluation/attachment. This risk is introduced/exposed by adding CLIENTS alongside USERS without any type check shown in the method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:310 — getResourceName is not extended for Clients, so client permissions show displayName (null) instead of the clientId, and a stale resource for a deleted client is not detected the way deleted users are.

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* extend client handling in `AdminPermissionsSchema#getOrCreateResource` by adding `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`, registering it in the schema map, and adding an explicit `resolveClient(session, id)` branch (mirroring the existing user logic). That directly addresses resource-name resolution and deleted-object detection via `name == null` handling. The finding references a `getResourceName` at line 310, but that method/change is not shown in the diff, and the stated behavior (clients not being handled at all) contradicts the visible additions for clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:359 — map-roles, map-roles-composite and configure are granted in one permission, so the test cannot show that each scope is enforced separately (e.g. configure alone could be what allows addComposites); map-roles-client-scope has no test at all.

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient the PR grants multiple client scopes in a single permission: `createPermission(client, myclient.getId(), clientsType, Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE), ...)`. Because `CONFIGURE` is bundled with `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`, the test can’t isolate whether `addComposites(...)` is enforced specifically by `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` vs being allowed by `CONFIGURE` or `MAP_ROLES`. adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:133 — All pre-grant deny assertions run with no policies at all, so they pass even if evaluation is broken; nothing tests an all-clients grant combined with a per-client resource or a NEGATIVE client permission.

The added tests in `PermissionClientTest` cover (a) no-permission default denies, (b) a single-client positive grant (`testManageOnlyOneClient` / `testConfigureOnlyOneClient`), and (c) a pure all-clients grant (`testManageAllClients`, `testViewAllClients`), but they do not cover the interaction/precedence between an all-clients grant and a per-client permission (e.g., per-client NEGATIVE overriding a global POSITIVE), nor any NEGATIVE client permission at all. However, the claim that the pre-grant deny assertions are meaningless is overstated: later in the same tests the granted-permission paths would fail if evaluation were completely broken, but the specific missing-combination/negative coverage is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap for the newly introduced fallback behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:101 — New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope / canMapClientScopeRoles has zero test coverage; PermissionClientTest never imports or grants it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` in `AdminPermissionsSchema` and wires it into `CLIENTS` resource type scopes, and implements `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel client)` to check `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`. In the updated tests, `PermissionClientTest` imports/grants `MANAGE`, `CONFIGURE`, `VIEW`, `MAP_ROLES`, and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`, but never imports or grants `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, nor is there any other added/modified test shown that exercises `canMapClientScopeRoles` behavior. This is a concrete missing test for newly introduced authorization logic, but not a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — Legacy remove-event listener is now gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, changing role/group/client removal cleanup behavior, with no test asserting the new gating.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly gates the provider event cleanup logic inside `AdminPermissions.registerListener` with `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java), whereas previously it always reacted to `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent`, and `GroupRemovedEvent`. This is a real, diff-grounded behavior change (cleanup no longer occurs when the feature is disabled). The diff adds/updates several FGAP tests, but none in the shown changes assert the new "only when feature enabled" gating for removal-event cleanup, so the finding about missing test coverage for this gating is supported by what’s visible here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:237 — Realm-wide hasPermission(scope) path backing canManageClientScopes/canView(ClientScopeModel) is untested; no test hits the /client-scopes admin endpoints under Clients permissions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces realm-wide permission evaluation via ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String scope) (used by canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel) to authorize client-scope operations based on the Clients resource type). The added tests in PermissionClientTest exercise client endpoints (create/update client, secrets, default/optional client scopes under /clients/{id}/...) but do not hit the realm-level /client-scopes admin endpoints nor explicitly cover the realm-wide hasPermission(scope) path for client-scope management/view. This is a specific coverage gap for newly added nontrivial authorization logic, not a demonstrated functional defect in the diff.
